styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Palaces, coffee houses and the Ringstrasse.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Klimt, the Kunsthistorisches and the MuseumsQuartier.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Schnitzel, cake and long café afternoons.

stays.why: Walk to St. Stephen's, the Hofburg and the Ringstrasse. Quietest at night; book early.
Across the Danube canal, near the Prater and the Augarten. Good U-Bahn links, better value.
Between the MuseumsQuartier and the Naschmarkt. Lively streets, easy walk to the centre.
Independent shops, bars and cafés. Young feel, 10–15 minutes on the U-Bahn to the centre.

food: Try a Wiener Schnitzel (veal or pork) with potato salad, and Tafelspitz (boiled beef) in a traditional Beisl.
Coffee houses are a ritual: order a Melange, sit long, and read the papers. Cake like Sachertorte or Apfelstrudel is normal mid-afternoon.
Naschmarkt on Saturday morning: stalls, spices and cheap snacks. Many stands close on Sunday.
Street food: a Käsekrainer sausage from a Würstelstand, around €5–7.
Book dinner ahead for popular places; many kitchens close around 22:00. Tipping is rounding up plus a little, said aloud.
more_time: Swap a museum morning for Schönbrunn Palace and its gardens, half a day with the U4.
Take a day trip to the Wachau valley or Baden by train; check times on the day.
Add a Danube evening: swim or walk at the Alte Donau, or cycle the Donauinsel.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the big palaces, two or three museums and a proper café afternoon without rushing.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 4°C, lows around -2°C. Pack a warm coat; museums and cafés are the plan.
Still cold, highs near 8°C. Fewer tourists and lower prices; expect some rain on about 9 days.
Warming to 11°C. Good for walking the centre; keep a rain layer for about 7 wet days.
Spring: highs near 16°C. Parks and gardens start to look good; about 9 rain days.
Lovely at 20°C but the wettest month, around 13 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
Warm at 26°C with about 12 rain days. Long evenings; outdoor cafés and the Donauinsel.
Hot peak: highs near 27°C, lows 17°C. Some afternoons are sticky; plan shade and water.
Similar to July, around 27°C and fewer rain days (about 9). Good for parks and day trips.
Comfortable at 22°C. A strong month for sightseeing; about 9 rain days.
Cooler at 16°C. Bring a jacket; good museum weather with about 10 rain days.
Cold and grey: highs near 9°C, lows 3°C. Christmas markets start late in the month.
Coldest with January: highs near 6°C, lows around 0°C. Dress in layers; about 10 rain days.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate: cold winters, warm summers, and rain spread through the year. Spring and autumn are the easiest months to walk the city.

items.title: Best months: April to June and September
items.text: Highs around 16–26°C. Comfortable for walking and palaces without summer heat.

items.title: Summer is warm, not extreme
items.text: July and August peak near 27°C with mild nights around 17°C. Some afternoons feel humid.

items.title: Winter is properly cold
items.text: December to February highs of 4–6°C and lows near or below freezing. Snow is possible but not guaranteed.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 7–13 rain days every month, most in May. Showers often pass; a small umbrella is enough.

items.title: Pack layers
items.text: A warm coat and gloves for November to March; light layers and a rain jacket for spring and autumn.

items.title: December is festive but cold
items.text: Christmas markets are outdoors. Wear boots and thermals, and warm up in coffee houses.

transit.best: Buy a 24/48/72-hour pass and use the U-Bahn and trams; the centre is flat and walkable.

modes.text: U-Bahn, trams and buses share one ticket. Buy a 24/48/72-hour pass or single fares around €2.60. Validate before riding; inspectors fine on the spot.
Buses and trams use the same ticket as the U-Bahn. Validate before riding.
Taxis are metered. Uber and Bolt both work in Vienna.
Driving is slow and parking is scarce. Skip the rental car in town.
The centre is flat and walkable. Bikes and e-scooters are easy to rent.
No ferries. The Danube is crossed by bridges and the U-Bahn.
